findings.text: Filesystem type registration maintains a global list keyed by exact name match. Registration validates an optional parameter description, rejects names containing a separator, rejects already linked objects and duplicate names, then appends and invalidates the cached listing. Unregistration removes a linked object, invalidates the cached listing, waits for readers, and reports success, while removal of an unlinked object fails.

Access to the filesystem registry and its cached string form is serialized by a dedicated spin lock with read side traversal allowed under that lock. Mutation paths hold the lock while checking or linking, advance a generation counter and clear the cached string with deferred freeing. One build variant makes invalidation have no effect.

Mount parameter descriptions are well formed when no two entries share a name unless one is a flag and the other is not. A flag entry is recognized by absence of a type descriptor. Conflicting duplicates cause a diagnostic and overall failure while scanning continues over the table.

Superblock wide writeback waiting requires the unmount semaphore already held, then takes the per superblock sync mutex and the writeback list spin lock under read side protection. Inodes are returned to the superblock list before dropping the spin lock so list membership stays consistent with writeback tagging, and references are taken under inode lock with protection held across the wait.

The wait covers only inodes present at entry by moving the superblock writeback list onto a temporary list. Untagged mappings and inodes in freeing or new states are skipped without waiting, with removal left to writeback completion. Per mapping error state is preserved for later reporting and the waiter yields the processor between inodes.
Anonymous block device numbers are released by returning the minor component to a global unnamed device allocator.

Two binary format handlers and one filesystem type are described. The misc filesystem has a fixed human readable name, allows user namespace mounts, creates contexts through a dedicated initializer that installs its context operations, and tears down through its kill routine. Each binary format descriptor references its owning module and its loader routine.

Boot and unload entry points install and remove binary format handlers and the misc filesystem type. Successful filesystem registration is followed by format insertion at the head of the search order. Removal unregisters the format and filesystem and then drains outstanding entry reclamation callbacks before module text can be freed. Script support registers and unregisters its format without a filesystem.
BPF based misc operations registrations link a list node with a pointer to operations, a link object, and a user namespace reference. A dedicated spin lock serializes the global registration list.

Four sleepable helpers for selecting interpreter, argument and flags are exposed as kfuncs owned by the misc module. Admission is limited to struct operations programs, with enforcement deferred while attachment state is unset and otherwise restricted to the load callback of a misc operations program. Initialization registers this set for the struct operations program type, and membership in that type is recognized by program type plus attachment to the misc operations descriptor.

Custom misc operations supplied through BPF must provide sleepable match and load callbacks, and validation fails if either is missing. Object names are copied with length checking and rejection of empty results. Default stubs report no match and success respectively for control flow integrity, and verification reuses base helper protocol with tracing context access rules.

BPF operations objects move from unregistered to registered on allocation of a tracking entry holding current user namespace and link, with insertion under lock after per namespace name uniqueness check, and remain until the matching operations and link pair is found and removed with release of namespace and memory. The operations type is published at boot under a fixed operations name with callbacks for validation, registration and member handling.

Helpers staging execution choice copy caller supplied path or argument into private memory before length, emptiness and form checks, then replace previously staged interpreter state while releasing old file and string references. Interpreter paths must be absolute and bounded, selected names must be non empty and within a small maximum and resolve against available interpreters, and flag combinations forbid unknown bits, forbid loader together with other modes, and forbid transparency together with argv preservation.

Script execution is accepted only for files starting with the two character magic sequence. The first line is located or, when no newline is present, truncation safety is established by requiring blank separated termination of the interpreter token. Leading and trailing blanks are trimmed, an optional single argument is isolated, inaccessible script paths are rejected, and accepted requests rebuild the argument stack with interpreter, optional argument and script path before opening the interpreter executable.

BPF helpers expose acquisition of a task executable file with a reference, release of a file reference, and rendering of a path into caller memory with left justification of the result. Empty destination size and path formatting failures are reported as errors with length returned on success.

BPF attribute access distinguishes read and write privilege. Reads are permitted only for user and security BPF namespaces after a read permission check. Writes are permitted only for the security BPF namespace after a write permission check, with missing inodes rejected. POSIX access control names are treated separately and excluded from the generic value path.

Dentry and file scoped BPF attribute helpers operate on dynamic buffers, validating writable access and permission before delegating to virtual filesystem get or set. Successful BPF driven sets emit a notification but intentionally skip the post set security hook to avoid reentering the same BPF path, mirroring the setsecurity behavior. Generic retrieval rejects POSIX control names and handlers lacking a get callback.

Extended attribute names are resolved by iterating the superblock handler table and matching the longest registered prefix by character comparison. Resolution requires attribute support on the inode, fails corrupt inodes as input output errors, applies empty remainder rules according to whether the handler defines a prefix, and reports unsupported operation when no handler matches. Effective prefix is the explicit prefix when present else the handler name, and iteration safely handles a null table.

In the routed configuration keyring destruction on superblock teardown, superblock deletion notification, and one variant of filesystem list string invalidation are defined as having no observable state change.

Stable interface facts include the misc filesystem type name, the requirement that staged interpreter paths are absolute, a small maximum length for selectable interpreter names, and a set of five execution flag options covering argv preservation, credentials, exec descriptor, transparency and loader substitution with stated incompatibilities.

Untrusted caller memory and script header contents are treated as racy. BPF setters duplicate inputs before validation and enforce termination and length limits to avoid time of check differences. Script parsing never executes a possibly truncated interpreter token and tolerates missing newline only when termination proves completeness, while argument truncation remains acceptable because the interpreter can reread the file.
